facts: Paige publishes proactive alerts to Nostr when the daily pipeline detects a rule change, proof update, or freshness warning.
Every alert carries a Satohash proof link — Paige never publishes an alert without an anchored proof.
Alerts are detection facts: 'something changed' — they never tell you what it means or what to do.
Five alert types: rule-change, proof-update, freshness-stale, new-pathway, pathway-closed.
Rule-change alerts fire when the official source page content hash differs from the baseline.
Proof-update alerts fire when intel:stamp re-anchors a program to a new Bitcoin block.
Freshness-stale alerts fire when a program is more than 45 days since last human research.
New-pathway alerts fire when a new pathway is added to a program in countries.json.
Pathway-closed alerts fire when a pathway is removed from a program in countries.json.
Alerts are published as Nostr kind 30078 replaceable events with hashtag filters.
Users subscribe to Paige's pubkey and filter by the 'motopass' hashtag to see alerts.
Portfolio-aware filtering is client-side: load portfolio from localStorage, match against alert #program tag.
Alerts are fire-and-forget: if no relay accepts, no retry spam.
No tracking: Paige does not know who subscribes. All filtering happens on the user's device.
The 'd' tag ensures dedup: one alert per program per change per day.
Alert generation reads audit_trail entries from countries.json and classifies them by field.
The alert generator script (generate-alerts.mjs) is wired into the daily-intel.yml pipeline after intel:stamp.

alert_types.rule-change: Official source page content changed — hash differs from baseline
alert_types.proof-update: Program re-anchored to a new Bitcoin block via Satohash
alert_types.freshness-stale: Program data is more than 45 days old — needs re-research
alert_types.new-pathway: New pathway added to a program in countries.json
alert_types.pathway-closed: Pathway removed from a program in countries.json

honesty_rules: Alerts are detection facts — 'something changed', never 'X now means Y'.
Every alert carries a Satohash proof link — no proof, no alert.
Alerts are fire-and-forget — no retry spam if relays are down.
No tracking — Paige does not know who subscribes.
No false urgency — alerts are informational, not actionable instructions.
Dedup by design — one alert per program per change per day.

member_scripts.how_will_i_know: Paige publishes proactive alerts to Nostr when the daily pipeline detects a rule change, proof update, or freshness warning. Subscribe to Paige pubkey in your Nostr client to see notifications for programs in your portfolio.
member_scripts.what_does_alert_mean: A rule-change alert means the official source page for a program has changed. It does not tell you what changed or whether it affects you. Verify the proof and check the program page for details.
member_scripts.can_i_filter_alerts: Yes. Subscribe to Paige pubkey and filter by the motopass hashtag. Your Nostr client can further filter by program name to show only alerts for programs in your portfolio.
member_scripts.are_alerts_proof_gated: Yes. Every alert carries a Satohash proof link. Paige never publishes an alert without an anchored proof. You can verify the alert independently.
member_scripts.what_is_freshness_alert: A freshness-stale alert fires when a program is more than 45 days since last human research. The data may be outdated — check the program page for the latest.
member_scripts.how_to_subscribe: In your Nostr client, add a subscription filter: authors = Paige pubkey, #t = motopass, kinds = 30078. You will see all MotoPass alerts in your timeline.
